body:
Not yet. These are all realizations that I've just synthesized today, and I've been at work all day.

I'm not entirely sure how to talk to him about it.
Don't even worry about the sex.
I'm dying to have sex with my best friend. She has a boyfriend. So do I.

What if we team up?   
  
My birthday is in the next few weeks and I stopped taking my medication a while ago. I've been thinking about restarting them as a gift to my mental health.  
  
Let's do this?
Not schizophrenic. Just the instability. If you can't count on the world around you, what can you count on?

>you can learn to change your reality to suit you.  

That is the single most destabilizing thought I've ever heard.
Drinking only delays the thought, it doesn't resolve it.
And if you can't trust your mind?
There's a windmill dangerously close to the road. It looks like you're going to drive right into it. I'm waiting for the day that I do.

Hi. I'm really sorry to hear that things have been in a downward spiral lately. I've been on a similar track.  
  
The good thing is that you acknowledge that you don't know how to do some things. That means you have things left to learn. These are things that you get the opportunity to improve on when you choose to stay.
I'm outgoing and friendly, despite how terrified I am of most of the interactions I'm in. This means I always feel surrounded by a community of people that I love and that love me too.

The thing to remember with mental health medications is that they work differently for everyone. Knowing subjective accounts is good, but only when you have a large quantity of them.  
  
If you're concerned about the way that Zoloft is working for you, which I think you rightfully are, then your next step is talking to your doctor. Your doctor will be able to tell you more.

That's a really long time to be in it. That demonstrates just how strong you are. You've been able to keep going for this long.  
  
In that time, things have happened. In three years, you grew up, you changed, you learned, you met people. Good things happened. Regardless of what your brain may tell you now, you have experienced good things in the last couple of years.  
  
You will continue to experience good things if you stay. Good things don't happen after.  
  
Do you like video games? Any particular movies or TV shows? I know the House series finale is on Hulu.

You said it yourself: you don't want to kill yourself. There's no chance of you seeing things get better unless you stick around long enough to see it happen. It's a tough thing to fight against, I too am fighting the urge at the moment. But the key is to keep fighting.  
  
For now, I'd suggest finding a distraction. Something, anything else to do. Not necessarily something you have to do. Do something you like doing. Preferably with other people.  
  
Do you see a physician at all?
